The results do not include a paper specifically about “Fernandes” Brazilian legal document segmentation beyond a retrieval-focused structural chunking approach. “Structural Segmentation for Brazilian Legal Document Retrieval” by Leandro Carísio Fernandes et al. studies structural segmentation of Brazilian legal acts by representing each document as a collection of hierarchical chunks, and compares several simplified core-chunk-based strategies for Brazilian legal retrieval. The paper reports improved dense retrieval versus whole-document indexing, while lexical retrieval does not consistently benefit; it also finds full hierarchy representation is not necessary because core chunks enriched with metadata can perform comparably or better. [1]

Related segmentation ideas for Brazilian legal text are addressed differently: “Legal Nugget Extraction for Granular Retrieval over Long Jurisprudential Texts” extracts short self-contained “legal theses” (“nuggets”) for granular retrieval and aggregates nugget hits back to document rankings, improving some jurisprudence benchmarks but not others. [5] “PRecG” segments legal judgments based on rhetorical roles and uses the segments to build graph-enhanced representations for precedent retrieval (but the paper is on Indian legal data). [8]
